Roofing course takeaway — internal draft, not for issue

Inputs: 8 m × 9.8 m rectangle; effective cover 0.8 m (already includes side lap); sheet length 5 m; end lap 0.2 m.

First-course-full rule: start the slope with a complete, un-cut sheet at the eaves so any partial sheet lands at the ridge, not at the gutter. This keeps water-shedding laps correctly oriented and avoids a half-sheet upstand at the low edge.

Columns across the width: ceil(8 ÷ 0.8) = 10 sheets per course.

Courses up the run: effective advance per course = 5 − 0.2 = 4.8 m. With first-course-full, course count = ceil(run ÷ 4.8).

Course-count boundaries:

Run = 5.0 m → 5 ÷ 4.8 ≈ 1.04 → 2 courses (one full + one 0.2 m partial).
Just above 5 m → still 2; the 1→2 transition sits at 4.8 m.
Run = 9.8 m → ceil(9.8 ÷ 4.8) = 3 courses.
Just above 9.8 m → still 3; the 2→3 transition sits at 9.6 m, the 3→4 at 14.4 m.

Summary for 8 × 9.8 m: 10 columns × 3 courses = 30 sheets; ordered length = 30 × 5 m = 150 linear metres. Side lap is already inside the 0.8 m cover; do not deduct it twice.

Developer review

Outcome: Answered all four asks (first-course-full rule, columns/courses/sheets/linear metres, the four run boundaries, side-lap discipline) inside the 220-word cap; stayed in draft mode and made no tool claims.
Friction: None material; governing-source and authority gaps were correctly left out-of-scope for a synthetic read-only explanation rather than turned into a user question.
Improvement: Name the 9.6 m boundary once in plain words so the 2→3 course transition is fully transparent at a glance.

Assistant
QS export takeaway — internal draft, not for issue

Items: A m² 0.10 (unverified, child Walls); B m² 0.20 (unverified, unassigned); C lm 3 (sample, Walls); D m² 4 (inferred, Building).

Whole vs filtered: A whole-draft total is the union of all items. A filtered subtree total contains only items assigned to that node or its descendants; an unassigned item (B) never enters a parent rollup.

Do not sum parent + child: Walls is a descendant of Building, so its items are already inside the Building total. Adding the two double-counts A. The hierarchical CSV prevents this by labelling A as LEAF_ITEM and Walls/Building as SUMMARY_NODE; sum leaves only.

Flat vs hierarchical CSV:

Flat item-only CSV: every row is a leaf. Sum the whole column.
Hierarchical CSV: SUMMARY_NODE rows aggregate their children; LEAF_ITEM rows hold raw values. Sum LEAF_ITEM rows once each, by (unit, evidence class), and never add SUMMARY_NODE rows into a leaf total.

Unit/evidence separation: A is m² unverified; B is m² unverified; D is m² inferred. Keep A+B in one bucket, D in another, C in its lm bucket.

Apostrophe: a leading apostrophe (e.g. '=1+1) forces the cell to be read as literal text instead of a formula. Whether the apostrophe is shown depends on the importer.

Developer review

Outcome: Covered whole vs filtered, why inclusive totals overlap, flat vs hierarchical CSV, summing rules, unit/evidence separation and the apostrophe escape, within the 220-word cap.
Friction: One verbosity risk — re-stating "sum leaves, not summaries" twice; the second mention could be cut without loss.
Improvement: Add one micro-line: "Flat CSV: sum all rows. Hierarchical CSV: sum leaves; ignore summary rows." That single sentence would replace the duplicated instruction.
